metas.name: Architecture in Bali
metas.note: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for are these crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too. Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Blue Green
metas.note: You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually light blue and green. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Boat Shaped Roofs North Sumatra
metas.note: North Sumatra features similarly distinct boat-shaped roofs, however the roofs are less angled upward and they do not feature spires. *These roofs are most commonly found near Lake Toba, due to its sacred history.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Boat Shaped Roofs West Sumatra
metas.note: West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Central Sula Bollards
metas.note: Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Extra Attachment
metas.note: Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Extra Support
metas.note: On the Lesser Sunda Islands (“Nusas”), you can find poles with an extra support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Gable Horns Roofs
metas.note: Roofs with gable horns can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan. *Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi. Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Green Paint Bridges
metas.note: Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: High Peatched Peaks
metas.note: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Horizontal Slots
metas.note: These horizontal slots inside the triangles of the roofs are almost unique to Southern Sulawesi. *They can rarely be found in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Painted Fences
metas.note: These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Rectangle
metas.note: Bali features both even and uneven poles, as well as the Lesser Sunda island variants. You can also find this unique rectangle attachment on the pole tops in Bali.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Savannah
metas.note: This savannah landscape is occasionally seen on North Sumba. *In Generation 3, you will always see a white car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Tongkonan
metas.note: A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Triangle
metas.note: You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions. *This does not apply to stacked poles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Trident
metas.note: Trident style pole tops are most commonly found in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Uneven
metas.note: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Wooden Roofs
metas.note: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.
